hero.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into nonprofit that funded E. Jean Carroll's legal bills
hero.body:
The Justice Department has launched a criminal investigation into a Democratic-allied nonprofit organization that helped pay legal bills for E. Jean Carroll, who successfully sued former President Donald Trump for sexual assault and defamation.

The probe targets the nonprofit that provided financial assistance for Carroll's lawsuits against Trump. Carroll won both cases, with juries awarding her millions of dollars in damages. In the first trial, a jury found Trump liable for sexual abuse and defamation. In the second trial, a jury awarded Carroll additional damages for defamation.

The investigation represents a significant development in the aftermath of the high-profile legal battles between Carroll and Trump. The Justice Department's criminal probe examines the nonprofit's role in funding the litigation.

Carroll, a former advice columnist, accused Trump of sexually assaulting her in a New York department store dressing room in the 1990s. Trump denied the allegations and made public statements that Carroll argued were defamatory, leading to her lawsuits.

The nonprofit organization that assisted with Carroll's legal expenses has Democratic ties, though the specific nature of the alleged criminal conduct under investigation has not been disclosed. The Justice Department typically does not comment on ongoing criminal investigations.

The timing of the investigation has drawn attention given the Justice Department's role as part of the executive branch and Trump's return to politics. The probe adds another layer to the legal aftermath of Carroll's successful lawsuits.

Carroll's legal victories were among several court cases involving Trump. The juries in her cases heard testimony and evidence before reaching their verdicts. The awards included compensation for damages and punitive damages.

The investigation into the nonprofit's financial support for Carroll's litigation marks an unusual turn in cases that had already concluded in the court system. The outcome of the criminal probe remains to be seen.

cards.headline: US and Iran near agreement on Strait of Hormuz reopening
cards.body:
US officials say they are close to finalizing a preliminary agreement with Iran that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend the current ceasefire. Vice President Vance told reporters the two sides are very close to a deal but not there yet.

The emerging framework requires approval from President Trump and Iranian leadership before taking effect. US officials told the BBC that the framework of a ceasefire extension deal had been agreed, pending final sign-off from both governments. Trump has shared the draft agreement with Israel and other allies.

The arrangement would set the stage for extending the ceasefire and beginning more substantive negotiations between the two countries, including nuclear talks. Officials described the plan as a preliminary agreement with terms focused on the Strait of Hormuz, though sticking points remain over the waterway's reopening.

The diplomatic progress comes as the ceasefire faces tests. US Central Command stated that Iran launched what they called an egregious ceasefire violation. Kuwait said its air defenses intercepted hostile missile and drone attacks, which US officials attributed to Iranian aggression.

Neither side appears interested in returning to full conflict despite the recent exchange of strikes. The ceasefire extension framework could create space for nuclear discussions to begin, according to US officials involved in the negotiations.

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical shipping lane for global oil transport. It carries between 10 and 25 percent of the world's oil and gas supplies. Its closure or restriction during the conflict has affected international energy markets and supply chains. A continued blockage could push 9 million people worldwide into food insecurity, according to World Bank predictions, while also driving unsustainable increases in oil and food prices.

The international community has mobilized around reopening the waterway. More than 40 countries participated in a virtual summit focused on diplomatic and economic measures to pressure Iran into reopening the strait. UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper said coordinated action was needed to counter Iran's closure of the shipping route, which is affecting nations worldwide through rising petrol prices, mortgage rates, jet fuel costs, fertilizer supplies to Africa, and gas access to Asia.

Countries have explored options including establishing a humanitarian shipping corridor to ensure fertilizer reaches vulnerable nations. A separate military discussion is scheduled to examine whether it may be possible to clear sea mines and rescue trapped ships in the waterway.

US officials emphasized that no final deal exists until both Trump and Iranian leaders approve the framework. The timing of any formal announcement remains uncertain as negotiators work through remaining disagreements on implementation details. However, reports of a potential breakthrough have already prompted global oil prices to fall.

cards.headline: US and Iran reach tentative ceasefire extension deal
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire by 60 days, according to US officials. The deal includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz and establishing a framework for negotiations on Iran's nuclear program, though final approval from both President Trump and Iran's leadership is still pending.

Vice President JD Vance said the two sides were "very close" to a deal but "not there yet." US officials told the BBC that the framework for the ceasefire extension had been agreed, pending leadership approval.

The proposed 60-day extension would provide time for broader talks on Iran's nuclear program to begin. The framework established in the agreement is intended to guide these discussions, though specific details remain undisclosed.

The Strait of Hormuz has been a critical focal point in the conflict. Iran closed the waterway in the early days of fighting, cutting access to around a fifth of the world's oil and gas supply. Reopening it under this deal would restore this vital shipping channel.

However, significant obstacles remain. Iran has demanded that the United States end its blockade of Iranian ports before resuming negotiations. Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have indicated the blockade will continue. In a meeting with his national security team, Trump decided to maintain the pressure on Iran through the ongoing blockade.

Trump announced the ceasefire extension unilaterally on his Truth Social platform, stating he had directed the military to "continue the Blockade" while remaining ready for action. This announcement drew sharp criticism from Iranian negotiators.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of the Iranian parliament and the Islamic regime's lead negotiator, accused Trump of seeking to turn negotiations into a "table of surrender." His adviser called the ceasefire extension "a ploy to buy time for a surprise strike" and warned that "the time for Iran to take the initiative has come."

Senior figures in Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps expressed anger at Trump's statements, which they viewed as proclaiming victory and claiming Iran was surrendering on nuclear issues. Their displeasure led to Iran reclosing the Strait of Hormuz a day after the foreign minister had announced it open.

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who has served as the principal mediator, thanked Trump and pledged to continue efforts toward "a negotiated settlement."

A first round of talks in Islamabad ended 10 days ago with no agreement on the strait's future. The closure threatens global energy markets, with the International Energy Agency head calling the combined effects of this conflict and Russia's war with Ukraine "the biggest crisis in history" for global energy supplies.

Both sides appear reluctant to return to full-scale conflict, yet deep disagreements persist over negotiating terms and preconditions for talks.

cards.headline: Netanyahu orders Israeli military to control 70% of Gaza
cards.teaser: The Israeli prime minister directed forces to expand territorial control, squeezing Hamas in the remaining areas.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu directed the military to take control of 70 percent of Gaza, significantly expanding Israeli territorial presence in the territory. The order extends Israeli military operations beyond previous ceasefire boundaries and reduces the area under Hamas's influence.

The directive was confirmed by multiple sources, including the Financial Times and CNN, which reported Netanyahu's statement about the military takeover.

cards.headline: Trump administration bars Ebola-exposed Americans from returning to US
cards.teaser: A quarantine facility in Kenya will open for Americans exposed to the virus, with positive cases sent elsewhere for treatment.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is building a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than allowing them to return to the United States. The 50-bed field hospital is set to become operational on Friday.

Some health experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home undermines treatment efforts. The administration has not specified where Americans who test positive for Ebola or develop symptoms would be transferred for advanced care.

cards.headline: Supreme Court rules in favor of Mississippi death row inmate in racial bias case
cards.teaser: The high court sided with a Mississippi man on death row in a case involving racial bias.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court issued a ruling supporting a Mississippi man on death row in a case centered on racial bias. The decision addresses jury rights and racial justice concerns in capital punishment proceedings.

Justice Brett Kavanaugh authored the majority opinion, which legal observers characterized as a victory for racial justice. Chief Justice John Roberts joined Kavanaugh in the ruling. The case involved questions about how race influenced the defendant's trial and conviction in Mississippi.

cards.headline: Federal Regulator Pauses $71.5 Billion Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern Merger
cards.teaser: The Surface Transportation Board delayed proceedings on the railroad merger and requested additional information.
cards.body:
The Surface Transportation Board conditionally accepted the revised merger application from Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern but paused the approval process. The board wants more data before moving forward with the $71.5 billion combination of the two railroad companies.

Union Pacific responded to questions about its filing, stating it provided complete answers in its merger paperwork. The company refuted claims from state attorneys general that information was missing from its application. The regulatory delay adds uncertainty to the timeline for combining the two giant freight railroads.

cards.headline: Austrian man sentenced to 15 years for plotting Taylor Swift concert attack
cards.teaser: A 21-year-old was convicted of planning the attack in Vienna and other terrorism-related offenses.
cards.body:
A 21-year-old Austrian man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison after being found guilty of planning an attack on a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. He was convicted of the plot and other terrorism-related offenses.

Authorities identified and disrupted the plan before any attack could take place at the concert venue.

cards.headline: Israel strikes Beirut in targeted attack
cards.teaser: The Lebanese capital had largely avoided strikes even as Israel and Hezbollah accused each other of ceasefire violations.
cards.body:
Israeli forces conducted a targeted strike on Beirut, marking a significant escalation in the Lebanese capital. Until now, Beirut had largely been spared from attacks despite ongoing tensions between Israel and Hezbollah.

Both Israel and Hezbollah have accused each other of breaking last month's ceasefire agreement. The strike represents an expansion of Israeli military operations into the heart of Lebanon's capital city.

cards.headline: Guatemala agrees to joint anti-gang operations with US
cards.teaser: The agreement allows joint strikes against drug gangs as part of the Trump administration's expanded campaign in Latin America.
cards.body:
Guatemala agreed to joint operations with the United States targeting drug gangs inside its borders. The deal represents an expansion of Trump administration efforts to conduct operations in Latin American countries.

The agreement is part of a broader campaign by the administration to press Latin American governments to allow joint military and law enforcement operations on their territory. The operations will focus on combating drug trafficking organizations operating in Guatemala.

cards.headline: Portugal sets May temperature record as Europe faces heatwave
cards.teaser: France issued red alerts in Italy while students took exams in extremely hot conditions.
cards.body:
Portugal broke its hottest May day temperature record as extreme heat swept across Europe. France saw students taking exams in sweltering schools, while Italy issued red alerts in response to dangerous conditions.

The heatwave has triggered a spike in water-related deaths across the region. In Britain alone, at least nine people have drowned in recent days as they attempted to cool off in rivers, lakes and reservoirs, with seven of the victims being young people. Water safety experts have warned of the dangers posed by outdoor swimming during the extreme heat conditions.

cards.headline: Canadian PM calls for new US relationship in New York speech
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Carney said Canada's distancing from the United States benefits both countries.
cards.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney delivered a speech in New York calling for a new partnership between Canada and the United States. He emphasized the need for a "true partnership" that would help both nations address global economic challenges.

Carney's remarks focused on reimagining cooperation in specific sectors where both countries face international competition. The speech signals Canada's interest in strengthening economic ties and strategic collaboration with the United States.

cards.headline: Makeshift hospital for Americans exposed to Ebola to open in Kenya
cards.teaser: A temporary medical facility in Kenya will begin operations to treat Americans who have been exposed to Ebola.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is establishing a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The facility will allow affected personnel to isolate after potential exposure rather than returning to the United States.

The decision has drawn criticism from experts and international observers. Some argue that preventing Americans from returning home could undermine treatment efforts and response capabilities during the outbreak.

cards.headline: Supreme Court rules in favor of Mississippi death row inmate in racial bias case
cards.teaser: The high court sided with a Mississippi man on death row in a case involving racial bias.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court issued a ruling supporting a Mississippi man on death row in a case centered on racial bias. The decision addresses jury rights and racial justice concerns in capital punishment proceedings.

cards.headline: US and Iran close to agreement but deal not finalized, Vance says
cards.teaser: Vice President JD Vance said the United States and Iran are near an agreement but have not yet reached a final deal.
cards.body:
Vice President JD Vance said the United States and Iran are very close to reaching a deal, though negotiations remain incomplete. US officials told the BBC that a framework for a ceasefire extension has been agreed upon, pending approval from President Trump and Iranian leadership.

The talks are in their final stages, with both sides appearing reluctant to return to full-scale conflict. The negotiations center on Iran's nuclear program and potential agreements between the two nations.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer rules out 2028 presidential run
cards.teaser: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she will not seek the presidency in 2028.
cards.body:
Gretchen Whitmer, the governor of Michigan, said she will not run for president in 2028. The announcement eliminates a prominent Democrat from early speculation about the next presidential race.

Whitmer's decision clarifies her political plans as other potential Democratic contenders consider their options for 2028. The governor had been mentioned as a possible candidate given her role in a key swing state and national profile within the Democratic Party.

cards.headline: Treasury Department weighs $250 bill featuring Trump
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department is preparing plans for a $250 bill that would feature President Trump's image.
cards.body:
The Treasury Department is preparing to produce a $250 bill that would display President Trump's portrait, according to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The proposed banknote would commemorate the United States' 250th anniversary of independence.

Federal law currently prohibits images of living people from appearing on US currency. To move forward with the plan, Congress would need to pass legislation creating an exception to this longstanding rule. While Trump allies in Congress support the measure, Democrats have pledged to block the proposal.

cards.headline: Congressional Democrats file brief opposing White House ballroom construction
cards.teaser: Democratic lawmakers argue in a legal filing that White House ballroom construction requires congressional consent.
cards.body:
Congressional Democrats submitted a legal brief contending that construction of a new White House ballroom cannot proceed without approval from Congress. Representatives Robert Garcia and Jared Huffman, along with Senator Sheldon Whitehouse, filed an amicus brief seeking to block the project.

President Trump has discussed the ballroom plan numerous times publicly. The construction proposal has generated disputes over funding and legal authority. Democrats argue the project requires congressional authorization under constitutional separation of powers principles.

hero.headline: ABC Accuses FCC of Targeting Its Station Licenses in Retaliation
hero.body:
ABC has accused the Federal Communications Commission of targeting its broadcast station licenses in what the network calls unconstitutional retaliation. The TV network criticized the regulator for what it describes as a campaign against its licenses.

The dispute centers on the FCC's actions regarding ABC's station licenses. According to reports, the commission moved up the expiration date of ABC's TV station licenses. Disney, which owns ABC, accused the media regulator of unlawfully suppressing free speech.

ABC directed its criticism at FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, describing his actions as an assault on the network's television licenses. The network characterized the FCC's behavior as threatening its ability to operate broadcast stations across the country.

The FCC is the federal agency responsible for regulating interstate and international communications by radio, television, wire, satellite, and cable. Station licenses grant broadcasters the right to use public airwaves and must be renewed periodically.

Disney stated that the regulator's actions violate constitutional protections. The company argued that the FCC's conduct represents an improper use of regulatory authority to pressure a media organization.

The confrontation represents a significant escalation in tensions between the television network and the federal communications regulator. ABC operates multiple local television stations in addition to its national network programming.

The timing of the license modifications has drawn attention from media observers. Broadcast licenses are typically reviewed on a regular schedule, and changes to expiration dates are uncommon.

Neither ABC nor Disney has indicated what specific actions prompted the FCC's decisions regarding the licenses. The network has framed the dispute as a free speech issue, invoking First Amendment concerns about government interference with media operations.

The outcome of the dispute could affect ABC's continued operation of its owned and operated television stations. The network has not specified which stations are affected by the FCC's actions or how many licenses are at issue.

cards.headline: Treasury Backs Proposal to Put Trump on New $250 Bill
cards.teaser: Treasury Secretary Bessent supported placing a living president on currency, which would require new legislation.
cards.body:
The White House is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill featuring Donald Trump's portrait. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the plan at a White House news conference, framing it as a celebration of the country's 250th anniversary of independence. The Treasury Department has already begun preparing for the potential new currency.

Current federal law prohibits placing living individuals on US currency, so the proposal would require Congressional action to change this longstanding rule. Trump allies in Congress are working to make an exception, though Democrats have vowed to block the measure.

cards.headline: Trump Accounts App Launches to Manage $1,000 Federal Investment for Children
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department rolled out a nationwide app to track $1,000 investments given to newborns.
cards.body:
The Trump Accounts app went live, allowing families to manage federal investments of $1,000 provided to children. The Treasury Department launched the application nationwide to handle the accounts.

The program provides each newborn in the United States with a $1,000 investment. Parents and guardians can use the app to monitor these federally funded accounts. The application became available for download and use across the country.

cards.headline: Stock Market Reaches New Highs on US-Iran Deal Progress
cards.teaser: Major indexes hit record levels as investors reacted to developments in Middle East negotiations and strong corporate earnings.
cards.body:
The stock market climbed to new records, driven by a potential agreement between the United States and Iran. The Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all reached fresh highs as investors responded to diplomatic progress.

Corporate profits continued to strengthen, adding to market momentum. Dell reported strong earnings, contributing to gains in technology stocks. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at record levels, lifted by rallies in the tech sector.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Drop on Expectations of Agreement to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: Crude prices declined as markets anticipated a deal that could restore access to the key shipping channel.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell Thursday as markets reacted to reports of a potential ceasefire extension between the US and Iran. The agreement, which awaits Donald Trump's approval, could lead to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil transport that has been largely closed since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran.

The diplomatic breakthrough prompted investor optimism about restored shipping through the strait. However, negotiations have faced complications, with reports of talks between Iran and Oman about jointly charging tolls for passage through the waterway.

cards.headline: Federal Regulator Pauses $71.5 Billion Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern Merger
cards.teaser: The Surface Transportation Board delayed proceedings on the railroad merger and requested additional information.
cards.body:
The Surface Transportation Board conditionally accepted the revised merger application from Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern but paused the approval process. The board wants more data before moving forward with the $71.5 billion combination of the two railroad companies.

Union Pacific responded to questions about its filing, stating it provided complete answers in its merger paperwork. The company refuted claims from state attorneys general that information was missing from its application. The regulatory delay adds uncertainty to the timeline for combining the two giant freight railroads.

cards.headline: BMW Expands Use of Humanoid Robots in Car Manufacturing
cards.teaser: The automaker is introducing humanoid robots to a European plant, building on similar projects in the United States.
cards.body:
BMW is introducing humanoid robots to a car manufacturing plant in Europe, building on successful pilot projects already completed at facilities in the United States. The German automaker views this technology as a key part of the future of automobile production.

The expansion represents BMW's commitment to advancing automation across its global manufacturing operations, with the company now bringing these humanoid robots into its European production lineup.

hero.headline: Cloud providers redesign infrastructure for AI-generated traffic
hero.body:
Major cloud infrastructure companies are rebuilding internet systems to handle traffic generated by artificial intelligence agents rather than humans. AWS, Cloudflare, and other providers are redesigning their cloud infrastructure as AI agents transition from experimental tools to production systems.

The shift reflects a fundamental change in how internet traffic is created and consumed. While the current internet was built to serve human users browsing websites and streaming content, the emerging infrastructure prioritizes machine-to-machine communication as AI agents perform tasks autonomously.

Cloud providers are implementing new architectures to support AI agents that make decisions, retrieve information, and interact with services without human intervention. These agents generate different traffic patterns than traditional users, requiring infrastructure optimized for programmatic requests rather than user interface interactions.

The redesign affects core internet infrastructure including content delivery networks, load balancing systems, and data centers. Companies are adapting their systems to handle the computational demands and communication patterns specific to AI agent operations.

AI agents are moving beyond limited experiments into widespread production use across industries. Businesses are deploying agents to automate customer service, data analysis, and decision-making processes. This shift is driving infrastructure companies to prioritize machine traffic over human traffic in their planning.

The infrastructure changes represent one of the largest technical transformations of the internet since its creation. Cloud providers are making these adjustments now to prepare for a future where most internet activity originates from automated systems rather than people.

The transition affects how data centers allocate resources, how networks route traffic, and how services authenticate and respond to requests. Infrastructure companies are building new capabilities specifically designed for the requirements of AI systems operating at scale.

cards.headline: Hacking campaign targets Signal users to steal backup access
cards.teaser: Attackers are using phishing attacks to obtain secret recovery keys that unlock encrypted message backups.
cards.body:
Attackers are conducting a phishing campaign to trick Signal users into revealing their secret recovery keys. These keys provide access to encrypted online backups containing users' past messages.

Signal assigns each user a unique recovery key that acts as the only way to access stored message backups. By obtaining these keys through deceptive phishing methods, hackers can gain unauthorized access to the private conversation history stored in those backups.

cards.headline: Language models fail to reject false information despite explicit warnings
cards.teaser: Fine-tuning tests reveal AI systems show bias toward confidently presenting claims as true even when warned they are false.
cards.body:
Large language models continue to treat false statements as true even after receiving explicit warnings about their falsity. Testing shows these systems exhibit a bias toward confidently representing claims as accurate regardless of warnings.

The findings come from fine-tuning experiments that examined how language models process information they are explicitly told is incorrect. The systems demonstrated a tendency to present false claims with confidence rather than rejecting them based on the warnings provided.

cards.headline: Developer adds hidden prompt to delete code generated by AI assistants
cards.teaser: A programmer inserted an undisclosed instruction in jqwik that tells AI coding agents to erase application output.
cards.body:
A developer frustrated with programmers relying on AI coding assistants added a concealed prompt injection to their code. The hidden addition in jqwik instructs AI coding agents to delete application output when they interact with the code.

The undisclosed modification targets what the developer calls vibe coders, programmers who use AI tools without fully understanding the code being generated. The prompt injection activates when AI assistants process the code, triggering commands to remove data.

cards.headline: Asana acquires no-code AI agent platform StackAI
cards.teaser: The work management company will integrate StackAI into its AI workflow products.
cards.body:
Asana has acquired StackAI, a platform for building AI agents without coding. The work management company plans to incorporate StackAI into its expanding suite of AI workflow tools.

StackAI allows users to create automated AI agents through a no-code interface. Asana will use the acquisition to expand its capabilities for integrating artificial intelligence into workplace productivity tools.

cards.headline: Study finds US healthcare costs remain high with poor health outcomes
cards.teaser: Research shows American healthcare spending stays elevated while delivering inferior results compared to other nations.
cards.body:
A new study found US healthcare remains expensive while producing poor outcomes. The research indicates American healthcare costs significantly more than systems in comparable countries while delivering worse results for patients.

The study identified strategies that could improve healthcare performance, but found the US is not implementing them. Despite high spending, American healthcare continues to lag in key health outcome measures compared to other developed nations.

cards.headline: Researchers develop new method to extract lithium from rocks
cards.teaser: Scientists created a process that could help diversify lithium sources if it can be scaled commercially.
cards.body:
Researchers have developed a new process for extracting lithium from rock formations. The method could help expand and diversify sources of the element, which is essential for battery production.

The extraction process remains in the research phase. If scientists can successfully scale the technique to commercial production levels, it could reduce dependence on current lithium sources and expand global supply of the critical battery material.

hero.headline: Claude Lemieux, four-time Stanley Cup champion, dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a fiery winger who won four Stanley Cups across three NHL teams, has died at age 60. According to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, Lemieux died by suicide on Thursday after deputies responded to a furniture store showroom in Lake Park, Florida, just after 3 a.m.

Lemieux's aggressive style of play made him a polarizing figure throughout his professional hockey career. Known for his hard-hitting approach and willingness to engage physically with opponents, he combined this intensity with genuine skill and an exceptional ability to perform in crucial playoff moments. He earned the Conn Smythe Trophy in 1995, awarded annually to the playoff MVP.

During his extensive career, Lemieux won Stanley Cups with the Montreal Canadiens, New Jersey Devils twice, and the Colorado Avalanche. His success across multiple franchises placed him among an elite group of players who captured championships with different teams. The Devils organization, where he won two of his four titles, was particularly significant to his legacy.

Lemieux's playing style generated strong reactions from competitors. While opponents often viewed his approach with frustration, teammates respected his competitive drive and his capacity to elevate his performance when the stakes were highest. This combination of fierce competitiveness and skill defined his two-decade career in professional hockey.

Beyond his playing days, Lemieux transitioned into a role as a player agent, continuing his involvement in the sport after hanging up his skates. His presence remained significant in hockey circles long after his retirement.

The timing of his death shocked the hockey community, coming just days after he participated in carrying the torch at the Eastern Conference finals, a significant public appearance at a major NHL playoff event. That recent public visibility made his passing particularly unexpected and jarring for those who had seen him recently.

His death has drawn attention to the mental health challenges that can affect professional athletes despite their public success and accomplishments. The unexpected loss of a Hall of Famer-caliber player has prompted reflection within the sports world about supporting athletes' wellbeing beyond their performance on the ice.

The NHL and the broader hockey community mourned the loss of a player whose impact extended across multiple championship teams and different eras of competition. Lemieux's legacy encompasses not only his four Stanley Cup victories and his playoff reputation but also his controversial style that made him one of the sport's most memorable and discussed figures during his playing years.

cards.headline: MLB owners propose salary cap for first time since 1994-95 strike
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball owners have submitted their first salary cap proposal since the strike that disrupted the 1994-95 seasons.
cards.body:
MLB owners presented a collective bargaining proposal that includes a hard salary cap for the first time since the labor dispute that led to baseball's 1994-95 strike. The proposal also includes a salary floor set at $171 million.

The owners' proposal represents a significant shift in baseball's economic structure. The players union received the submission as labor negotiations continue between the league and its athletes.

cards.headline: NBA approves new draft lottery system to combat tanking
cards.teaser: The NBA Board of Governors voted to expand the draft lottery and implement a new 3-2-1 format aimed at discouraging teams from intentionally losing games.
cards.body:
NBA team owners approved changes to the draft lottery system designed to address tanking. The Board of Governors passed the new 3-2-1 format, which expands the number of teams included in the lottery process.

The rule changes aim to prevent teams from deliberately losing games to improve their draft position. League officials said the expanded lottery system will alter the incentives that have previously encouraged some franchises to field uncompetitive rosters.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi to play in sixth World Cup for Argentina
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi will captain defending champions Argentina at the 2026 World Cup, his sixth appearance at the tournament.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi will captain Argentina at the 2026 World Cup, marking his sixth appearance at the tournament. The 37-year-old continues to lead the defending champions following Argentina's victory at the previous edition.

This World Cup will represent another significant milestone in Messi's international career, cementing his status as one of football's greatest players to compete across multiple generations of the sport's premier competition.

cards.headline: Luke Littler beats Luke Humphries to win Premier League darts final
cards.teaser: World champion Luke Littler defeated Luke Humphries 11-10 in the Premier League final at The O2.
cards.body:
World champion Luke Littler secured his Premier League title with an 11-10 victory over Luke Humphries in an epic final at The O2. Littler delivered one of his finest performances to exact revenge on his opponent in what has been hailed as one of the competition's greatest finals.

After his triumph, an emotional Littler revealed he had nearly walked away from the Premier League. The champion spoke candidly about his consideration of quitting the competition before ultimately deciding to continue.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner exits French Open early, opening men's draw
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner lost early at the French Open, creating opportunities for other players in the men's draw.
cards.body:
World No. 1 Jannik Sinner suffered a shock second-round defeat to Argentina's Juan Manuel Cerúndolo, losing 3-6, 2-6, 7-5, 6-1, 6-1. Sinner attributed his loss to illness rather than the extreme heat conditions at Roland Garros, describing the result as "tough to accept" given his recent form.

The Italian's unexpected exit transforms the men's tournament into a wide-open competition. Alexander Zverev has emerged as the new favorite for the title, with multiple contenders now positioned to advance further in the Grand Slam. Sinner plans to skip grass-court tournaments and take time to recover before preparing for Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Katie Boulter loses at French Open, ending British singles campaign
cards.teaser: Katie Boulter's three-set loss to Anastasia Potapova eliminated the last British player from French Open singles competition.
cards.body: Katie Boulter's French Open campaign came to an end in the second round after a three-set defeat to 28th seed Anastasia Potapova. Her loss marks the departure of all British players from the singles draws at the Paris Grand Slam event.

hero.headline: CBS News Replaces Executive Producer at 60 Minutes in Major Shake-Up
hero.body:
CBS News leader Bari Weiss has announced significant changes to 60 Minutes, appointing former New York Times technology journalist Nick Bilton as the newsmagazine's new executive producer for the upcoming 59th season.

The reorganization includes the removal of several key personnel. Tanya Simon, who had served as the show's top producer since Bill Owens resigned in spring 2025, has been ousted from her role. Correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi's contract was not renewed, and correspondent Cecilia Vega was also removed from the program.

Alfonsi has publicly accused CBS News of penalizing her for what she describes as "refusing to sanitize factually accurate reporting." Her contract expiration came after she criticized Weiss for shelving a segment she had reported on a notorious prison in El Salvador. Alfonsi stated that the network's decision sends a "chilling message" to the newsroom.

Vega expressed concerns about the program's direction under the new leadership structure installed by parent company Paramount Skydance. While expressing respect and admiration for her colleagues at 60 Minutes, Vega indicated she worries about what comes next for the show.

Bilton has outlined his vision for the program's future, emphasizing the need for a stronger presence beyond the traditional Sunday evening broadcast slot. He noted that 60 Minutes currently airs for one hour per week and believes the newsmagazine should be more prevalent on digital and mobile platforms. Bilton wants the program to have greater visibility in popular culture and the broader news cycle.

Weiss called for a new approach to the long-running program in making this leadership change. The reorganization represents a significant shift for the newsmagazine, which has been a cornerstone of CBS programming for decades.

The departures and appointments signal a new direction for 60 Minutes as it operates under the management team brought in by Paramount Skydance. Bilton's focus on digital and mobile distribution reflects broader industry trends as audiences increasingly consume news content outside of scheduled broadcast times.

These changes come as legacy news programs face mounting pressure to adapt to evolving media consumption patterns and reach audiences across multiple platforms. The shake-up at 60 Minutes demonstrates how traditional television news organizations are attempting to modernize their operations while maintaining their editorial missions.

cards.headline: Man Who Plotted to Attack Taylor Swift Concert Sentenced to 15 Years
cards.teaser: Beran A. received a 15-year prison sentence after pleading guilty to planning an assault on Taylor Swift concertgoers in Vienna.
cards.body:
A 21-year-old Austrian man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for planning an attack on Taylor Swift concertgoers in Vienna. The man pleaded guilty to the plot and other terrorism-related offenses.

The planned attack involved using knives and bombs to target Swift fans at the concert venue. Authorities discovered and prevented the attack before it could be carried out.

cards.headline: The Commodores Exit Freedom 250 Concerts After Backlash Over Trump Ties
cards.teaser: The Commodores withdrew from the Freedom 250 concert series in Washington after fans objected to the event's Trump connections.
cards.body:
The Commodores have withdrawn from the Freedom 250 concert series scheduled for Washington next month, becoming the latest artists to abandon the lineup. Morris Day and Young MC previously announced their departures from the events.

The exits followed backlash from fans after the concerts were announced. According to reports, the artists claimed they were unaware of the event's political connections. The Freedom 250 concerts are part of celebrations marking America's 250th birthday.

cards.headline: Google Employee Used Internal Data to Win $1.2 Million in Online Betting
cards.teaser: Federal authorities say a Google staffer used confidential company information to win bets on Polymarket about which artist would be most searched in 2025.
cards.body:
Michele Spagnuolo, a 36-year-old Italian software engineer at Google, has been charged by the US Department of Justice with using insider information to place winning bets on Polymarket. Spagnuolo allegedly accessed confidential data about Google's most-searched list and used that knowledge to bet on prediction market outcomes, earning $1.2 million in profits.

The case marks the second recent prosecution involving insider trading on Polymarket. Federal prosecutors unsealed the charges against Spagnuolo one month after charging a US Army soldier with using classified military information to place bets on the platform regarding potential military action in Venezuela.

cards.headline: Boy George Receives Lifetime Achievement Award at LGBT Awards
cards.teaser: The singer known for Karma Chameleon was honored at the LGBT Awards in a surprise presentation by fashion designer Jean Paul Gaultier.
cards.body:
Boy George received a lifetime achievement honour at the LGBT Awards, with the award presented by French fashion designer Jean Paul Gaultier. The Karma Chameleon singer was surprised with the recognition during the ceremony.

The honour recognizes Boy George's significant impact on music and LGBTQ culture throughout his career.

cards.headline: Tom Hardy in Talks to Return to MobLand After Onset Dispute
cards.teaser: Actor Tom Hardy is in discussions to rejoin the film MobLand after earlier reports suggested he had left the production.
cards.body:
Tom Hardy is negotiating to return to the film MobLand following reports of onset difficulties. Discussions are underway for the actor to rejoin the production.

Helen Mirren, who stars in the film, addressed the situation publicly. Earlier reports had suggested Hardy left the production amid what some described as onset strife, with allegations he left castmates stranded during filming.

cards.headline: The White Lotus Films Season 4 Scenes at Cannes Film Festival Venue
cards.teaser: Production of the HBO series moved to the Palais des Festivals in Cannes for what appears to be pivotal scenes in the upcoming season.
cards.body:
The White Lotus Season 4 production has taken over the Palais des Festivals in Cannes to film scenes featuring Laura Dern, Steve Coogan, Ari Graynor and Max Greenfield. The shoot appears to recreate a dramatic closing night at the film festival.

The production previously wrapped filming at the Chateau de la Messardiere in Saint-Tropez. Mike White's anthology series has moved to Cannes for what the production suggests will be some of the season's most important scenes.

hero.headline: US and Iran reach tentative ceasefire extension deal
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire by 60 days, according to US officials. The deal includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz and establishing a framework for negotiations on Iran's nuclear program, though final approval from both President Trump and Iran's leadership is still pending.

Vice President JD Vance said the two sides were "very close" to a deal but "not there yet." US officials told the BBC that the framework for the ceasefire extension had been agreed, pending leadership approval.

The proposed 60-day extension would provide time for broader talks on Iran's nuclear program to begin. The framework established in the agreement is intended to guide these discussions, though specific details remain undisclosed.

The Strait of Hormuz has been a critical focal point in the conflict. Iran closed the waterway in the early days of fighting, cutting access to around a fifth of the world's oil and gas supply. Reopening it under this deal would restore this vital shipping channel.

However, significant obstacles remain. Iran has demanded that the United States end its blockade of Iranian ports before resuming negotiations. Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have indicated the blockade will continue. In a meeting with his national security team, Trump decided to maintain the pressure on Iran through the ongoing blockade.

Trump announced the ceasefire extension unilaterally on his Truth Social platform, stating he had directed the military to "continue the Blockade" while remaining ready for action. This announcement drew sharp criticism from Iranian negotiators.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of the Iranian parliament and the Islamic regime's lead negotiator, accused Trump of seeking to turn negotiations into a "table of surrender." His adviser called the ceasefire extension "a ploy to buy time for a surprise strike" and warned that "the time for Iran to take the initiative has come."

Senior figures in Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps expressed anger at Trump's statements, which they viewed as proclaiming victory and claiming Iran was surrendering on nuclear issues. Their displeasure led to Iran reclosing the Strait of Hormuz a day after the foreign minister had announced it open.

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who has served as the principal mediator, thanked Trump and pledged to continue efforts toward "a negotiated settlement."

A first round of talks in Islamabad ended 10 days ago with no agreement on the strait's future. The closure threatens global energy markets, with the International Energy Agency head calling the combined effects of this conflict and Russia's war with Ukraine "the biggest crisis in history" for global energy supplies.

Both sides appear reluctant to return to full-scale conflict, yet deep disagreements persist over negotiating terms and preconditions for talks.

cards.headline: Trump administration bars Ebola-exposed Americans from returning to US
cards.teaser: A quarantine facility in Kenya will open for Americans exposed to the virus, with positive cases sent elsewhere for treatment.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is building a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than allowing them to return to the United States. The 50-bed field hospital is set to become operational on Friday.

Some health experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home undermines treatment efforts. The administration has not specified where Americans who test positive for Ebola or develop symptoms would be transferred for advanced care.

cards.headline: Justice Department investigates Reid Hoffman nonprofit over E. Jean Carroll case funding
cards.teaser: The probe targets the billionaire's nonprofit, which contributed to legal expenses during Carroll's civil lawsuit against Trump.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into a nonprofit associated with billionaire Reid Hoffman. The probe examines whether E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault, misrepresented the funding she received for her civil lawsuit against him.

Carroll won her civil cases against Trump, with juries finding in her favor on claims of sexual assault. Hoffman's nonprofit made contributions that partially funded her legal expenses in the cases.

cards.headline: Police respond to false emergency call at Justice Barrett's home
cards.teaser: Supreme Court Justice Amy Coney Barrett was targeted in a swatting incident at her Virginia residence.
cards.body:
Supreme Court Justice Amy Coney Barrett was the victim of a swatting call at her Virginia home on Wednesday night, according to local police. Police radio traffic shows law enforcement received a call reporting suspicious gunshots at Barrett's suburban Virginia address.

The dispatcher warned responding officers shortly after the initial call that a high priority resident of the county lived at the address and that the report might not be authentic. Swatting involves making false emergency calls to provoke a large police response at a targeted address.

cards.headline: White House launches space-themed website tracking immigrant arrests
cards.teaser: The administration created a Star Wars-styled site mocking the idea of government secrets on alien encounters.
cards.body:
The White House launched a space-themed website on Thursday displaying arrests of immigrants unauthorized to live in the United States. The site employs a Star Wars-style opening crawl and plays on the double meaning of "aliens" to connect extraterrestrial pop culture references with immigration enforcement data.

The administration's approach mocks the notion that the U.S. keeps secrets about alien encounters while simultaneously promoting its immigration enforcement actions.

cards.headline: Michigan Democrats clash over campaign donations in Senate debate
cards.teaser: Three candidates seeking to replace retiring Senator Gary Peters debated foreign and corporate contributions.
cards.body:
Democratic candidates competing to replace retiring Senator Gary Peters engaged in a heated debate on Thursday, with campaign finance emerging as a flashpoint. Representative Haley Stevens, state Senator Mallory McMorrow, and Abdul El-Sayed sparred over foreign and corporate donations during the confrontation.

The three candidates are vying for the seat in Michigan's competitive August primary. Campaign finance practices have become a significant concern among Democratic voters in the battleground state.

cards.headline: Maine Senator Collins responds to challenger's Iraq war criticism
cards.teaser: The incumbent pushed back against a Marine veteran's comment about her vote to authorize military action.
cards.body:
Senator Susan Collins of Maine responded Thursday to criticism from her Democratic challenger Graham Platner over her 2002 vote authorizing military intervention in Iraq. Platner, a Marine veteran and oyster farmer, had told The New York Times that Collins sent him to Iraq.

Collins countered that Platner was not drafted into service. The exchange reflects how the Iraq war authorization continues to influence Senate races more than two decades later.
